descriptions.text: South Korean cryptocurrency exchange GDAC said on its official website that it was hacked and lost nearly $13 million. On April 9, the hackers moved nearly $13 million, or 23 percent of their total custody assets, from the GDAC hot wallet to an unidentified wallet. Hackers stole nearly 61 bitcoins (BTC), 350.5 ethers (ETH), 10 million wemix tokens (WEMIX), and 220,000 USDT.

GDAC disclosed unauthorized withdrawals from its hot wallets on April 9, 2023, leading to losses reported at roughly $13 million across BTC, ETH, USDT, and WEMIX. Public reporting and later forensic reconstructions point to compromised wallet signing access, but GDAC did not publish a technical postmortem or a confirmed intrusion vector. GDAC reported that attackers transferred assets from exchange-controlled hot wallets to external addresses. The public record does not establish the initial intrusion path or provide a confirmed forensic explanation. Hackers made off with 61 BTC, 350.5 ETH, 10 million WEMIX, and 220,000 USDT from a hot wallet belonging to the South Korean cryptocurrency exchange GDAC. Altogether, the assets are notionally worth around $13 million. The stolen assets represented 23% of funds custodied on the GDAC exchange. GDAC halted deposits and withdrawals shortly after the attack, and stated that they had reported the exploit to South Korean law enforcement to investigate.
